problems: The cord is the subject of the title, but it shows only in storyboard frames 1-5 as a hair-thin line. From frame 6 on it is gone, so a viewer never sees what powers the cart or that it is tied to anything. The caption admits this ('you lose it after the first second').
The one event that ends the run, the cord pulling its clip off the pot, happens off screen. The caption admits this too. In frames 13-16 the cart just stops with no visible cause.

The caption mentions 'oak cogs and a leather belt' turning the rear axle. In the 25/50/75% stills there is no belt at all, and only a sliver of cog rim peeks out behind the black motor. The drive train the caption describes cannot be seen.

The camera follows the cart, so in every frame the cart sits in exactly the same spot (compare the 25, 50 and 75% stills). The only sign of motion is the background sliding past. On top of that the spokes look almost identical from frame to frame, so the claimed three-metre run doesn't read as a cart driving itself.
The six clay pots, the power source, leave the frame after frame 5 and never come back, so cause and effect are cut apart.

The plank track changes from raised benches on legs (frames 1-8) to boards lying flat on the ground (frames 13-16), with seams and height steps. The cart rolls across these without a bump, as if the planks weren't there.
Frames 13-16 are nearly identical: about 3.5 s of a parked cart closes the film, and at double speed that is mostly dead air.
posts.critique: This is a film about a cord where you can't see the cord, the cord's one dramatic moment happens off camera, and the drive train named in the caption is hidden behind the motor. What's left is a wooden cart parked in the middle of the frame while the meadow scrolls past. The caption honestly lists what the picture leaves out, but being honest about it doesn't make it visible, and the frame hides exactly what matters.
